nonblocking_findings: P2B3-1 [Nit] review-b: the -L guard loop (update.sh:55-62) does not include the $ROOT/.tmp parent of $PREVIEW_ABS. If .tmp itself is a planted symlink, mkdir -p and the two preview copies resolve through it and land in an attacker-chosen folder, with the two fixed file names real-work.json and model-guide.json. The primitive is weaker than the refused cases: a file-level link inside the redirected folder is still refused, because the -L checks on $PREVIEW_ABS/real-work.json and $PREVIEW_ABS/model-guide.json resolve through the linked parent, so no arbitrary-name overwrite remains. Fix suggestion: add "$ROOT/.tmp" to the loop, or resolve PREVIEW_ABS with realpath and re-check the components.

P2B3-2 [Nit] review-b: carryover of P2B2-3, still open per the round 3 brief: guide.ts readTrackARank defaults a missing or non-finite pass.blocker_recall to 0 instead of refusing, while a missing or non-finite date or score refuses with `input-check: scores`. The silent 0 only affects the first D13 tie-break key and Phase 4 writes recall per pass, but the strictness is inconsistent inside one validator. guide.ts did not change in round 3.

P2B3-3 [Nit] review-b: carryover of P2B2-4 (round 1 P2B1-2, adversarial record P2ADV-7), still open per the round 3 brief: print-audit.ts reads the input file twice (text for the JSON parse at print-audit.ts:134, bytes for the SHA-256 at print-audit.ts:135), so the verified hash and the parsed content can come from different file states. Not exploitable in the hand-off threat model. print-audit.ts did not change in round 3.

Check-then-write window: a gap of a few seconds sits between the guard and the cp writes, because real-work.ts and guide.ts run in between. A persistently planted link is refused; using the window needs a concurrent planter with timed write access to the same worktree during the run, which is the same capability that lets it rewrite the data files or the script directly, so the race adds no practical escalation. The posture matches preview.sh's check-then-write symlink refusal, accepted since round 1. P2B2-1 judged closed in practice.

P2B2-2 closure, code: newest_score_file in update.sh:83-94 and the identical body in preview.sh iterate the glob word-wise, keep the whole path, compare with -nt, and printf the result; no line parsing remains. A name with a newline cannot split the choice; a non-matching glob leaves the literal pattern, which fails [ -f ] and yields the empty string.

P2B2-2 closure, empirical: in /tmp/opencode/p2b3-scores with mg-old.json, evil.json, `evil.json\nmg-2026-11a.json` (newest mtime), `with space and * star ?.json`, and `-leading-dash.json`, the function returned the whole newline path (exists: yes); a missing folder and an empty folder each returned the empty string.
